title: Independent verification: certify Eisenstein scalar floor over all flat pairs
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Independent verification of PR2017; no new numerical bound.** This package certifies its sharp scalar cost 40 using a direct binary-matrix rank argument. It reconstructs an explicit 80×80 binary witness and checks rank domination on all 595,984 ordered pairs of the 772 line-spanned flats. A written closure argument covers every support pair; rank subadditivity then covers every fitting binary matrix and every finite rectangle decomposition, including asymmetry and cancellation.

The new implementation does not import PR2017's Hermitian arithmetic, rank routines, or sampled traversal. It uses a complete generator-set traversal, XOR elimination, and exact prime-field rational ranks justified by integer minor bounds. The pinned PR798 coordinate generator is shared. There are 22,950 strict rank drops, including a concrete rank-four/rank-two example, so equality under reduction is never assumed.

This adds complete independent evidence for the decisive rank bridge behind the newly closed scalar E8 route. It does not audit physical pricing, the block-linear extension, or the full multiplication theorem. No κ, selected frontier, or upstream source changes.

## Task and overlap

Base `a878f5c65605ffde1dd4ca06a9c919e7803734cc`; actual task `01a1335e-7a24-73c3-a549-9bcb5496a363`; OS assignment seed 77, independent-verification track. `TASK.json` refines the independent-moment card to this pricing obstruction.

PR2017 (`5950e7896b8825a2c167ee63836251b3096060f8`) supplies the theorem and witness. PR798 supplies the geometry and original clique-bound pair table; this certifies a different binary witness inequality. PR2022's incorporated general orthogonal-frame result remains separate. PR801 concerns format ceilings. Discussion2028 concerns Walsh shear profiles. Source pins and overlap limits appear in `SOURCES.json` and `VALIDATION.md`.

The final refresh completed at 18:41 UTC: 347 open PRs and 722 Discussion records, complete pagination, no warnings. PR2017 and PR2022 retain the exact merged heads above. New PR2066 concerns Gaussian hyperplane reciprocity and does not overlap this Eisenstein certificate. No pinned coordination issue existed, so the claim is local.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/eisenstein-binary-rank-audit-seed77/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_EISENSTEIN_BINARY_RANK_AUDIT`.

Normal and optimized stable CPython 3.15.0 runs pass; the explicit repository Python 3.12 manifest also passes. All flat pairs, sharp row stars and five semantic negative controls pass. A relocated read-only run passes; source, certificate and receipt corruptions fail. The pinned predecessor replay, baseline binding check, selected-record check and five selected-record unit tests pass.

The generated expected receipt is a regression aid, not independent evidence. The proof is a finite exact certificate plus written coverage and rank arguments; it has no proof-assistant or independent human review yet. No unrelated global suite or selected supplier cold replay was run.

Charles Bethin, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in the independent model, implementation, proof exposition and checks. New work is Apache-2.0; predecessor files and notices are unchanged.

## Open next questions

The README records the next scope boundary: specify and fully price a changed nonlinear-message or physical-sharing contract before a new search. Adding scalar totals or changing the fitting matrix does not escape PR2017. No qualifying changed contract is supplied here.
